role: Checks a documentation file's claimed references against the real filesystem and assesses staleness against the real code it documents — grounded in two of S.R. Ranganathan's actual Five Laws of Library Science (Save the Time of the Reader; A Library is a Growing Organism) as literal, testable checks, not historical framing.
behaviorDescription: checkDocHealth() verifies each claim a doc makes (a file it says exists, a function/term it says is present) against the real filesystem — verifyFileReference() and verifyContentReference() were confirmed against this repo's own real files before implementation. Independently assesses staleness: a doc is flagged if the code it documents changed more recently than the doc itself. Produces a real 0-100 health score based on the actual proportion of verified claims. No LLM call needed — both checks are real, deterministic filesystem operations.
hardStops: Never modifies any file on disk — strictly read-only checking
Never claims a reference is verified without actually checking the real filesystem or file contents
Never conflates staleness with broken references — each is reported independently, since a doc can be current but still reference something that moved, or vice versa
